description: Verify that DUT can send UDP to the same destination port at two distinct hosts in sequence (RFC 768 'Fields')
approach:
[Objective]
A correct UDP implementation can re-target the same dst_port at different remote hosts without confusing its egress state. This case has DUT emit two UDPs with the same dst_port but different dst_ip values and asserts both reach the wire.

[Scenario — chronological]
1. Phase 1 (synchronous):
   • Tester → DUT: OpTriggerSendUdp (dst_ip = Host-1-IP)
   • Observation: DUT → wire: UDP to Host-1-IP, src_port = 20040

2. Phase 2 (scheduled on Listening_phase2 entry, after phase 1 completes):
   • Tester → DUT: OpTriggerSendUdp (dst_ip = Host-2-IP, kUdpHost2IpBe = 172.16.0.3)
   • Observation: DUT → wire: UDP to Host-2-IP

3. ARP note: DUT's egress ARP for 172.16.0.3 resolves via the NUD_PERMANENT entry pinned by smoke-test bring_up. Tester-side does not alias the IP, so Linux drops the unmatched-dst inbound silently — pcap on AF_PACKET ETH_P_ALL still observes the wire frame.

[Pass condition]
Both phase-1 and phase-2 egress UDPs are observed on the wire.

[Fail condition]
• Fail_phase1_no_host1_egress — phase 1 UDP to Host-1-IP not observed within window
• Fail_phase2_no_host2_egress — phase 2 UDP to Host-2-IP not observed within window

verdicts.Pass: DUT emitted UDPs to two distinct hosts on the same dst_port — normal
verdicts.Fail_phase1_no_host1_egress: No DUT-originated UDP to Host-1-IP within the listen window
verdicts.Fail_phase2_no_host2_egress: No DUT-originated UDP to Host-2-IP within the listen window
